page.overview:
What is Enter Sandman?

Enter Sandman is the first song and lead single off of the Black Album. The single achieved platinum certification for more than 1,000,000 copies shipped in the United States, spurring sales of over 30 million copies for Metallica and propelling Metallica to worldwide popularity. The song was written by Kirk Hammett, James Hetfield, and Lars Ulrich.

Enter Sandman's lyrics describe childhood fears, nightmares, and losing innocence. It uses the Sandman, a mythical figure who brings sleep, to symbolize how people face or give in to these fears, often seen through a child's prayers as they grow up. Although the traditional Sandman is supposed to bring good dreams, the song takes a darker turn, highlighting the fear of going to sleep and encountering frightening "monsters under the bed" and "nightmares of war" as innocence slips away into the night. "Enter Sandman" is arguably Metallica's most popular song to date.

Say your prayers, little one Don't forget, my son To include everyone I tuck you in, warm within Keep you free from sin 'Till the Sandman he comes

Sleep with one eye open Gripping your pillow tight
